question: In Samira Kohli v. Prabha Manchanda (2008), the Supreme Court of India held that a doctor may perform additional surgical procedures beyond those consented to without fresh consent, provided the procedures are in the patient's best interest and there is no time to obtain consent.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is actually FALSE. In Samira Kohli v. Prabha Manchanda (2008), the Supreme Court held that the doctor's removal of ovaries (during a laparoscopy consented to for a different purpose) was an assault. Best-interest justification does not override the requirement for informed consent except in genuine life-threatening emergencies.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. The Supreme Court in Samira Kohli held the opposite: even in intraoperative situations, a surgeon cannot extend the procedure to non-emergency findings without prior consent. The patient must consent to each procedure in advance. 'Best interest' does not substitute for autonomous consent in non-emergency circumstances.
